docs.title: Pokémon Rising Ruby & Sinking Sapphire
docs.text:
What is this?

A searchable version of the documentation for Drayano's Rising Ruby and Sinking Sapphire (v2.1.0), the enhancement hacks of Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire. The hack and its documentation are Drayano's work; see About for credits.

Warning

This wiki was AI generatedI from the documentation Drayano released with the hack, combined with vanilla game data. Some details may be wrong or missing. When in doubt, trust the original documents, and please report mistakes on GitHub.

PokédexAll 721 Pokémon with stats, abilities, moves, locations and every change made in the hack. Wild PokémonEncounter tables for every route, cave, city and Mirage spot. TrainersEvery trainer's team, rematch rosters and detailed boss battles. Boss BattlesGym Leaders, Team admins, rivals, the Elite Four and the Champion in full detail. General ChangesStats, types, abilities, evolutions, moves, items and shops. FAQExp. Share, the DexNav, legendaries, the legal-moves version and more.
  • Official release thread (download and install notes)
  • This wiki on GitHub

docs.title: About this wiki
docs.text: This is a hobby project: a browsable, searchable wiki for Drayano's Pokémon Rising Ruby and Pokémon Sinking Sapphire, inspired by the Platinum Renegade Wiki by Frederic Dlugi.

docs.title: How it is made
docs.text:
Everything on this site is generated by a small Python pipeline that lives in the GitHub repository:

  1. tools/parse_docs.py reads the six documentation text files that ship with the hack (Pokémon, area, attack, evolution, item and gift/static changes) and turns them into structured data.
  2. tools/base_data.py builds the vanilla Omega Ruby / Alpha Sapphire baseline (base stats, types, abilities, TM/tutor/egg moves, evolutions, held items, move data) from the PokeAPI CSV tables, reconstructing Generation 6 values where later games changed them.
  3. tools/generate_site.py merges the two, so every Pokémon page shows the hack's data with vanilla values alongside anything that changed, and writes the Markdown pages.
  4. Material for MkDocs turns the Markdown into this site.

Level-up moves come entirely from Drayano's documentation. TM/HM, tutor and egg moves are the vanilla ORAS lists plus the additions the documentation describes. Base stats, abilities and types are vanilla unless the documentation lists a change.

docs.title: Building it yourself
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 tools/build.py        # fetch data, parse docs, download sprites, generate pages
mkdocs serve                  # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000/

docs.title: Credits
docs.text:
• Drayano created Rising Ruby / Sinking Sapphire and wrote the documentation this wiki is built from. The original thread is on Project Pokémon.
  • The logos were made by kojiyomi.
  • Vanilla game data comes from PokeAPI, and sprites from the PokeAPI sprites repository.
  • Site design by Material for MkDocs; sortable tables by tablesort.
  • The idea and layout follow the Platinum Renegade Wiki.

docs.title: Legal
docs.text: Pokémon and all related names, characters and sprites are © Nintendo, Creatures Inc. and GAME FREAK inc. This is an unofficial fan site with no affiliation to them or to Drayano. No ROMs or game files are hosted here.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Answers to common questions, mostly drawn from the notes in Drayano's documentation.

docs.title: Which version of the hack does this wiki cover?
docs.text: The documentation bundled with v2.1.0 (October 2016), the latest release. Rising Ruby and Sinking Sapphire share the same documents; the version differences are the same as between Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire (Team Magma or Team Aqua, Groudon or Kyogre), and the wild lists are shared.

docs.title: Should I turn off the Exp. Share?
docs.text: Yes, unless you want an easier game. Trainer levels were designed for a full team of six without the Exp. Share. You still receive it in Petalburg Woods and it is on by default, so switch it off from the bag.

docs.title: Why does the DexNav not show every Pokémon on a route?
docs.text: Each area has data for 10 or more species, but the DexNav only has a fixed number of slots, so it cannot display them all. The species that do appear are the ones earlier in the internal lists, and Drayano arranged these so that Pokémon with the most desirable hidden abilities are the ones you can search for.

docs.title: How do encounter rates work?
docs.text: Every grass, cave or sand area has at least ten species with a 10% chance each. Areas with eleven species have two at 5% instead; those are marked as rare on this wiki. Pokémon in grass have a fixed level for the route, which the White and Black Flutes can modify.

docs.title: Where are the starters and other horde-only Pokémon?
docs.text: Some species such as the starters of every region, Eevee, Plusle and Minun only appear in horde battles. Trigger hordes with Honey or Sweet Scent; early Pokémon that already know Sweet Scent include Bellsprout, Surskit, Swirlix and Spritzee.

docs.title: What are the DexNav-only Pokémon?
docs.text: The species listed under the DexNav method only appear late in the game, after the Groudon or Kyogre conflict in the Cave of Origin is over. They replace the foreign Pokémon that appeared on routes in the original games and are usually high-levelled evolved forms of something native to that route.

docs.title: Where are the legendary Pokémon?
docs.text: Most legendaries live on the Mirage spots, with a fixed set per terrain type (forest, cave, mountain, island) regardless of which island you visit. See the Mirage Forest, Mirage Cave, Mirage Mountain and Mirage Island pages. The static legendaries from the original games (the Regis, Rayquaza, the soaring encounters and so on) were kept, with higher levels; see gifts and static encounters.

docs.title: What do the asterisks on moves and abilities mean?
docs.text:
• * (one asterisk): the Pokémon can learn this move in the official games, but not by level up. It comes from egg moves, TMs/HMs or tutors. These moves are also present in the legal-moves version.
  • ** (two asterisks): the Pokémon cannot normally learn this move or have this ability at all. These are removed in the legal-moves version of the hack.

docs.title: What is the "legal moves" version?
docs.text: An alternate set of files that leaves out everything marked with two asterisks, so that Pokémon can be transferred or used without illegal movesets. Boss trainers have an alternate file too, with their illegal moves replaced by legal options. A version of the evolution file without the lowered evolution levels is also offered, but level-up movesets assume the lowered levels.

docs.title: What is the DllField.cro file and why does it matter?
docs.text: The gift and static encounter changes (perfect-IV starters and fossils, higher-level legendaries, the soaring encounters) live in a modified DllField.cro. Using it requires a loader that can patch the RO module, which Luma3DS and Citra can do but Gateway and HANS cannot. Without the file the game still works; you just do not get those particular changes.

docs.title: How do trade evolutions work now?
docs.text: Nothing needs to be traded. Pokémon that evolved by plain trading now evolve by level-up with high friendship or at a set level, whichever comes first. Trade-with-item evolutions now use the item like an evolution stone. Karrablast and Shelmet evolve by levelling up with the other species in your party. Trading still works as well. See evolution changes.

docs.title: Where do I buy evolution items and Mega Stones?
docs.text: Evolution stones are sold at the Slateport Poké Mart and Fallarbor Poké Mart; trade items such as the King's Rock and Metal Coat are at the Slateport Market; later items such as the Electirizer and Reaper Cloth are on the third floor of the Lilycove Department Store. Mega Stones appear in every Poké Mart once you have six badges, with more after eight. Salamencite and Diancite are held by wild Shelgon/Salamence and Diancie instead. See items and shops.

docs.title: Why can't I buy vitamins or X items?
docs.text: Shop inventories are limited in size, so vitamins and X items were dropped to make room for evolution items, Mega Stones and TMs. Vitamins can still be bought from the Battle Resort stalls; X items that are not found on the ground are no longer available.

docs.title: Who do the Battle Resort trainers mimic?
docs.text: The post-game trainers at the Battle Resort copy the teams of famous trainers from other regions, such as Cynthia, Lance and Diantha, as well as rematches that mirror Hoenn's own Gym Leaders. See the Battle Resort page.

docs.title: I found a mistake on this wiki
docs.text: The pages are generated from the documentation, so errors are usually either typos in the original documents or bugs in the generator. Please open an issue on GitHub.

docs.title: General Changes
docs.text:
Rising Ruby / Sinking Sapphire changes a great deal beyond trainer rosters and wild encounters. This section collects every documented change by category; each Pokémon's own page also lists its changes at the top.

From Drayano's documentation

In this document you'll find any changes made to the abilities, types, stats, held items, TM/HM compatibility, evolution method and level up moves to any individual Pokémon.

Level up moves are listed for every Pokémon, regardless of whether they've been changed or not. However, a large majority are edited, usually taking the approach of rearranging the level up order to make them more accessible to use by bringing important moves earlier or shrinking gaps between level up moves (think of how Eevee and its evolutions had their level up moves changed in B2/W2).

Most Pokémon have also been given additional moves in their level up pools; some of these are egg moves, move tutor or TM/HM moves that they can learn normally anyway, but can be hard to access in the context of the main game of OR/AS. There are some Pokémon that have also been given entirely new moves, abilities or TMs to play with (e.g. Megahorn Beedrill, Hurricane Sigilyph).

You can identify these new (and thus illegal in the usual games) additions by the asterisk system.

No asterisk means the Pokémon always can learn this move by level up, have this ability etc but it may be at a different level, be a hidden ability etc.

One asterisk (*) means the Pokémon is able to learn this move but not ordinarily by level up, and is most likely pulled from egg moves, TMs/HMs or move tutors. These moves are available in the full version as well as the legal only one.

Two asterisks (**) means the Pokémon is unable to obtain this ability or move ordinarily, and is completely illegal outside of the context of this hack. The legal moves only version of the a/1/9/1 GARC file omits all of these moves. Levels may be adjusted to fill the gap left by a removed move but are not documented. There are two specific cases that are documented with what they've changed into.

Additionally, a location on where to obtain a Pokémon (or what to evolve if not) is listed for each species, though you'll want to check out the wild document for more context.

docs.title: Evolution changes
docs.text:
From Drayano's documentation

This document covers any changes made to the way a Pokémon evolves. The Pokémon modified can be split into two distinct sections.

Any Pokémon with a trade evolution has been modified so that they no longer need to be traded to evolve. There are three distinct subtypes of this evolution:

  • Pokémon that needed to be traded with an item can now use that item like an evolution stone. Evolution items can be found in Slateport Market and Lilycove Department Store, with some exceptions like the Prism Scale (found on Corsola).

  • Pokémon that need a trade with no additional requirements now have a particular level at which they evolve. However, they can also evolve by happiness, keeping the 'any level' evolution they had before. It depends which one you reach first!

  • Pokémon that need to be traded with another Pokémon to evolve are now able to evolve by having that other Pokémon in the party and levelling up. It doesn't make a whole lot of sense, but it's the best we've got!

Please note that these new evolution methods are in addition to the trading way, meaning that trading the Pokémon will still evolve it as before.

The other type of evolution change is a Pokémon evolution level reduction, as a lot of Pokémon have an evolution level that's too high to keep up with the pace of the game. The majority of Pokémon affected by this change are from Unova where the evolution levels were incredibly high, but levels have also been reduced for Pokémon from the other regions that are caught fairly early but still have an evolution level hovering around 40. Zweilous still holds the title of having the latest evolution, but now evolves at 59 instead of 64 before. All new numbers and the amount subtracted from the old number are listed below.

A version of the evolution GARC is available without evolution level reductions is available if preferred. However, level up moves for Pokémon affected by this have been modified to assume that they evolve at the levels listed here.

docs.title: Gifts & static encounters
docs.text:
From Drayano's documentation

This document covers any changes made to the Gift Pokémon you receive as well as any static encounters within the game e.g. the Kecleon you encounter throughout the game, many legendary Pokémon and even the Wild Pokémon you encounter when Soaring in the Sky.

To see these changes, you need to include the DllField.cro file when building your game. However you will only be able to actually use these changes if you're playing with a method that is able to 'patch the RO module', else your game will crash upon trying to launch it. This means for Gateway and HANS users you can't use these changes, but Luma3DS or Citra users should be able to include it with no problems whatsoever.

docs.title: Item & shop changes
docs.text:
From Drayano's documentation

This document covers any changes made to items such as usability or price, as well as changes to what the PokéMarts and markets around Hoenn are selling.

The changes to PokéMarts are key to evolving many of the new Pokémon you can get as they will sell you evolution stones and items. You need to use the code.bin file in the exeFS and if not using HANS, also make sure no OR/AS patches from the eshop are installed to see these mart changes. (The same also applies to text edits but those aren't as important.)

PokéMarts also sell a few Mega Stones for a hefty price that you weren't able to get before defeating the Elite Four in OR/AS. This includes every Mega Stone with the exception of Salamencite and Diancite, which can be found as held items on Shelgon or Salamence and Diancie respectively.

From Drayano's documentation

Most Pokémon are obtainable quite early on and everything besides the legendaries can be found before you get seven badges, so there's plenty of variety to enjoy. Ice-type Pokémon are a bit sparse due to the region's climate, but for any other type you should have plenty of options to keep yourself happy.

docs.title: Wild Pokémon
docs.text:
Every area's wild encounters in Rising Ruby / Sinking Sapphire, taken from Drayano's area documentation. Pick an area below, or open a Pokémon's page to see everywhere it can be found.

From Drayano's documentation

This document contains a listing of the wild Pokémon and/or trainers found in almost every area in RR/SS. It is possible to obtain all 721 Pokémon within the game, with most Pokémon appearing wild (but generally not Pokémon that have already evolved twice, with some exceptions such as Pidgeot and Clefable).

Every area with grass/walking/sand etc has at least 10 wild Pokémon, each having a 10% chance of appearing on any encounter. Some areas have 11 Pokémon instead, in which case two will only appear with a 5% rate. These 5% Pokémon are shown with an asterisk next to their name. Pokémon appearing in grass have a static level for that route, though the Black and White Flute items can modify these.

Some Pokémon are only available through horde battles, such as starter Pokémon, Eevee, Plusle and Minun. As usual, you can trigger horde battles through the use of Honey or Sweet Scent; a number of Pokémon can be found early in the game that will already have Sweet Scent, such as Bellsprout, Surskit, Swirlix and Spritzee.

Pokémon listed next to the DexNav label only appear late in the game after the Groudon or Kyogre conflict in the Cave of Origin has been resolved. They replace the foreign Pokémon that appeared in many routes in OR/AS; in this game they're usually high levelled evolved forms of one species normally found in the route.

Legendary Pokémon are kept out of the way, with a selection of each located on a particular type of Mirage Island. You will find the same set of legendaries on a type of island (Island, Mountain, Cave, Forest) regardless of which island it actually is. Why are they there? Who knows. Maybe they're surprisingly real evolutions. Maybe they are the Ditto who are also native to these islands, but have somehow permanently transformed into this mysterious Pokémon. Maybe there's just nowhere else to put them. Who knows?!

A consequence of the large number of Pokémon in each area is that you will not be able to use the DexNav with all of them. Unfortunately despite each area having data slots for 10+ Pokémon the DexNav seems to have predetermined slots for any Pokémon and won't actually be able to fit them all on the screen. The ones that do appear are those earlier on the internal wild lists, so I've arranged things such that Pokémon with more desirable hidden abilities are more likely to appear on the DexNav. It's unfortunate, but at least in regards to egg moves, most Pokémon will get their useful ones by level up anyway!

The trainers for each route are also listed, with their Pokémon and accompanying levels shown. For special trainers such as Gym Leaders and the Elite Four, an extra section is shown with their Pokémon in higher detail, including abilities, held items and movesets. Some of these trainers do have new moves that are obtainable outside of this hack; an alternate trainer file is offered where these moves are replaced with legal options.

Trainer rematches are also shown for each route under a rematch column. The number next to their names refers to how many badges you need to obtain to unlock that trainer roster, e.g. a (2) means they'll start using those Pokémon if you rematch them after obtaining the Balance Badge in Dewford. (C) refers to champion and will be their team after clearing the Pokémon League the first time around.

One last thing to note is that the trainer levels throughout the game have been designed assuming you have a full team of six Pokémon and YOU ARE NOT USING THE EXP. SHARE. You still gain the Exp. Share in Petalburg Woods and it's set to on by default, so remember to toggle that unless you happen to be training an entire team of slow levellers or something.
